subject: Re: Performance SLO / Private VPC — network qualification follow-up (ACME)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: John Carter <john.carter@acme.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 Jul 2028 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Performance SLO / Private VPC — post-call recap and next steps

Thanks again for the call earlier, John — good session. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can progress the private/VPC qualification for ACME's performance SLOs.

Key SLO targets you gave on the call:
- 95th pct latency target: <= 90ms for short completions (~128 tokens)
- Burst throughput goal: 250 qps sustained for inference path (with autoscale to 500 qps)
- Concurrency per-session: up to 150 concurrent streams; streaming responses required for low-latency UX
- P50 internal processing budget end-to-end (client -> inference -> response): <= 60ms

Network / infra constraints you mentioned:
- Private VPC peering to our on-prem edge via IPsec VPN (primary)
- Expected egress path through ACME firewall; additional NAT layer adds ~5-10ms per hop
- Internal region: us-west-2, with a secondary site in us-west-1 for DR

What we need from ACME to validate performance SLOs on the private deployment:
1) Network diagram (logical + egress/NAT points) and any upstream firewall rules that could affect MTU or TCP window sizing.
2) Expected RTT from your app hosts to the peering IPs (traceroute/mtr outputs welcome).
3) VPN configuration (IKE versions, cipher suites) and whether you allow UDP ports for accelerated tunnels.
4) Sample request profile: average tokens per request, typical prompt size, and streaming chunk interval (if any).

Next steps / timeline:
- You share the network diagram and traceroute by EOD Wed (7/19) — we'll run a lab with a dedicated test job and provide a latency heatmap and suggested tuning (MTU, TCP, keepalive).
- If network looks good, we schedule a short (1-2 hour) on-site VPN test window the following week to measure real streaming latency at scale.

Attachments: I attached our private-deploy network checklist for reference.

Thanks — Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0123
Redwood Inference

Appreciate the recap, Marissa — that aligns with what we discussed. Quick responses inline:

- Network diagram: attaching a current logical diagram; will confirm the egress NAT hop count (we have 2 NATs in front of the public egress). Attached: acme-network-diagram.pdf
- Traceroute: I'll run traceroutes from our primary app cluster (10.10.2.0/24) to the peering IPs and send results by EOD Wed.
- VPN config: We use main IPsec tunnels (IKEv2) with AES-256-GCM; I can share the config snippet.
- Profile: avg prompt ~60 tokens, avg completion 120 tokens, we expect 200-300 rps during peak with spiky bursts. Streaming chunk interval roughly 50-100ms client-side.

We can open a maintenance window next Wednesday (7/26) morning for the test.

Thanks — John

john.carter@acme.com | (646) 555-4411

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: John Carter <john.carter@acme.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 19 Jul 2028 08:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance SLO / Private VPC — post-call recap and next steps

Awesome, thanks John — got the diagram. A couple of follow-ups after a quick review:

1) NAT hops: the extra NAT and firewall could add variability at the tail; can you confirm if there is any per-flow (stateful) inspection that would close idle connections under 60s? If so, we may need a keepalive tweak to prevent handshakes during bursts.
2) MTU / fragmentation: I see a transit link through an ISP-managed firewall. Can you confirm MTU (we've seen MSS clamping at 1400 in a similar setup) — please send if you have a known MTU on the VPN path.
3) For the traceroute, please include UDP and TCP (if possible) so we can compare.

Dev — looping you in to coordinate the lab test: during the test window we want to run 3 scenarios:
- Baseline long-poll streaming at 100 qps for 30m (validate p50/p95 latency)
- Load climb to 300 qps sustained for 10m (check autoscale behavior and tail latency)
- Burst test: short 1min bursts to 500 qps while keeping many concurrent streams (150)

Can you confirm we have a test harness that will mimic 50-100ms client chunk intervals and can produce the token lengths John provided?

John — if you can drop the traceroute outputs and the vpn-config-snippet.txt in the Drive link you shared, we will triage and propose any TCP/VPN parameter adjustments before the window.

Best,
Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference)

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, John Carter <john.carter@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 19 Jul 2028 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance SLO / Private VPC — lab test plan and harness

Thanks for the context — I can run the harness. Quick notes:
- Test harness: we'll use our streaming benchmark tool (redwood-loadgen) which supports chunked streaming at configurable intervals down to 20ms. I will configure scenarios to match Marissa's list.
- Metrics we'll capture: p50/p95/p99 latency, end-to-end RTT from client emulator, TCP retransmits, and application-level reassembly delays.
- For the bursting to 500 qps, we'll do a ramp (0->500 over 60s) and a hard spike to simulate sudden traffic.

I'll need the traceroute outputs and a sample VM IP from ACME to anchor the test. Also please confirm if we should originate traffic from our public test IPs or via a peer tunnel endpoint — latter preferred if you want to measure the exact production path.

I'll prepare a runbook and share it here by EOD today.

- Dev

--
Dev Patel
Staff Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

- MTU: our VPN path clamps to 1400; we can try to adjust but will need change window with network ops.
- Firewall: stateful inspection will drop idle flows after 45s.
- We can originate test traffic from the peer tunnel endpoint (10.200.5.12) during the window on 7/26.

I'll keep the 7/26 AM window reserved — tell me what time works for you.
